items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: how can Jeff’s role be made better, is he dominating too much or is he — because a lot of times our fourth person is usually our melody player

ctx.x: When you set about writing new compositions, does the fact that you had three or four fourth members affect the way you’re thinking about new work?

Not so much. Like I just write a lot. And I’m always screwing around with the banjo and stuff pops out and then I try to figure out what’s going to be good for the group. And a lot of times I just take what I think is the best song and what makes it the best song to me is hard to put my finger on but I’ll just have something and I’ll think well this is — there a bunch, I might have twenty things that I come up with, this one I think is special. It’s usually something about the melody or the chords that’s…

player who’s willing to fit into the group and find a way to make the whole group sound good. And he’s actually the guest sort of. He shouldn’t be the dominant figure. He should be an equal fourth at best. Or right in there. Because I mean the other three guys have been together for sixteen years. He’s only been here for — I mean it’s a delicate balance. And yet he needs to come forward and be strong and be a powerful musician that can stand up there with us and be dominant as well. So it’s a very tricky position…
